comment: Agent proposals (cause, edge record, whether the change looks intended) merged into annotations.template.json as `proposed`. Never a decision: the owner sets `decision` in annotations.json. Keys are annotation row ids.

R1:added:http.h1_header_timeout:<absent>.note: New knob SSE_H1_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS (default 120 s; 0 or unparseable keep the default). No family sets it. Behaviour: idle keep-alive, headless and partial-head HTTP/1.1 connections are closed after 120 s; the platform edge's upstream pool idle is unmeasured (edge record #12's risk).

R1:value:cli.absorb_concurrency:6->None.note: The three v1 absorber options lost their clap defaults and became Option (accepted but ignored; a supplied value logs one IgnoredAbsorberOptions warning). Inert on both sides: rc.4 set AbsorberConfig.{pass_bytes, small_pass_bytes, concurrency} and never read them. 2026-09-13, before the hardening program, so no edge record.

R2:NO_EFFECT_AT_VALUE:STREAMS_DEBUG_EXIT.note: Read by both sides (http.debug_exit = value == "1"); the family's 0 equals the unset default, so neither removal nor perturbation changes anything. Not a difference.

R2:NO_EFFECT_AT_VALUE:STREAMS_DEBUG_TIMI.note: Read by both sides (http.debug_timing = value == "1"); 0 equals the unset default. Not a difference.

R4:notice:new:ABSORB_PASS_BYTES are depr.note: Seen only in the merge-trap probe (region-server plus the rc.4-era ABSORB_PASS_BYTES=67108864). A Compute project that still holds the name boots and logs this one warning; the value had no effect at rc.4 either.

R4:notice:gone:ABSORB_GLOBAL_BUDGET_BYTE.note: rc.4 warned when the default 64 MiB absorb budget was floored to one worst-case frame build (96.2 MiB). The floor still applies at HEAD: the resolved absorbBudgetBytes (/v1/debug/absorb) is 100859904 on both sides, and HEAD states it in the INFO 'memory budget' line. Only families without the compute-1g profile (defaults, platform-e2e) hit the floor. Removed by the R10 refactor on 2026-09-06, before the hardening program.
